notes.summary: Established an unverified proof draft of M1–M3 and all-point resolved-nef fiber constancy using the actual BJ varying-class decreasing net, one dominating curve model, fixed background support, and correctly signed Green corrections. The descended scalar is usc.
notes.detailedSummary: Numerical triviality survives algebraically closed field extension by finite-data curve specialization and constant Euler characteristics. For each fixed smooth proper fiber curve over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued auxiliary field, a single graph-dominating semistable model carries every varying canonical reference. Its constant composite factors scheme-theoretically through the extended section. Background curvature coefficients are nonnegative fixed-support degree functionals tending to zero. Correct Green corrections converge uniformly to zero; boundary finite-intersection comparison passes the decreasing original net without assuming the corrected functions decrease. Geometrically connected fibers, separate residue-field extensions, and finite curve-morphism chains identify every analytic fiber value. All combined applications remain unverified drafts.
notes.text:
Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero; X reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective; L an actual ample rational line bundle; and π:Y→X projective birational, with Y smooth irreducible projective, factoring through normalization. Auxiliary curve fields are complete, algebraically closed and NONTRIVIALLY valued. These are unverified proof drafts. No singular EP, onto descent, or countable Runge theorem is granted.

Numerical specialization. Let Z be projective over k, Ω/k algebraically closed, and a:T→ZΩ a fixed proper integral curve morphism. Spread its projective equations, morphism charts and finite identities to a finitely generated integral k-algebra A⊂Ω. Shrink once for generic flatness and further for geometric integrality of the fibers. The generic fiber is geometrically integral because its extension to Ω is integral. For each fixed line bundle D, its pullback and the structure sheaf are finitely presented and flat over A. Proper flat Euler-characteristic constancy gives constant χ(Dt) and χ(OTt), commuting with field extension. Their difference is the curve degree. Choose a closed point of the remaining base; its residue field is k. If D is numerically trivial on Z, the specialized degree is zero: a nonconstant curve morphism contributes its generic degree times the degree on its image, and a constant morphism contributes zero. Therefore deg(a*DΩ)=0. Only this curve and this D are spread out; infinitely many bundles are not simultaneously descended.

Degree consequently annihilates the numerical kernel and defines a real linear functional on finite-dimensional N¹(Z)R, hence a continuous functional. This proves numerical triviality is preserved under algebraically closed extension without Picard convergence. The same specialization proves nefness ascends; extending each old curve and preserving its Euler-characteristic degree proves reflection. Ampleness of an actual line bundle uses fpqc ampleness, rather than a nefness inference.

M1 on the actual net. Fix s∈Xan, F=H(s), a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued extension K/F, and a smooth proper connected curve f:C→YK with constant composite to XK. Write R=K°. Its residue field is algebraically closed and contains k. For bounded genuine φ∈PSH(Y,π*L), use BJ Definition 4.1 itself:
φi∈H_R^gf(Li), φi↓φ, c₁(Li)→π*c₁(L).
This is a directed net with varying rational bundles. Since every φi dominates a bounded function, it is finite everywhere, so its sections have no common zero and Li is semiample. No approximation on the fixed π*L is assumed.

Take the flat schematic graph closure of f in one projective curve model times the constant model YR. BE5.13 supplies its map to YR and exact model-metric pullback. BE4.5 supplies finite presentation. Its relative integral closure inside the prescribed generic fiber C is finite and has reduced special fiber by BE4.20, used specifically because K is algebraically closed and nontrivially valued. This is not asserted for an arbitrary nondiscrete valuation ring; BE4.21 records the failure of that generalization.

The semistable model must dominate this graph. The graph and its relative closure are integral, proper and flat, with generic global functions K. Stacks0AY8 applies over the normal integral Spec R: properness, reduced source, dominance of every generic point and the generic global-function condition are all satisfied. Its special fiber is connected. Euler-characteristic constancy for every twist of a relatively very ample bundle makes its special Hilbert polynomial equal to the generic linear polynomial. Thus its maximum dimension is one. In a reduced finite-type scheme a zero-dimensional irreducible component is an isolated open-and-closed point; connectedness excludes it. All special components therefore have dimension one. The resulting flat finitely presented scheme is a multipointed R-curve with empty marking in Temkin’s definitions, with smooth semistable generic fiber.

Temkin’s actual stable-modification theorem applies. Its generically étale proper alteration has a generic component with finite separable field extension of K, which equals K because K is algebraically closed. The resulting K-point extends to an R-section by properness. Pull back the stable modification along this section. This gives a projective semistable R-curve Cmodel with an actual generic-fiber identity map to the chosen graph. Completion at an element 0<|a|<1 gives an admissible proper formal model. BPR’s formal-model/vertex-set correspondence permits finite type-II subdivisions removing loops if strict semistability is desired; these are dominating refinements and preserve the graph map. Existence of an unrelated semistable model is not used.

Every canonical Li reference pulls from this same constant YR model: Mi=fmodel*(Li⊗R). BE5.10/5.13 identify its model metric with the literal pulled canonical metric on f*Li, including original trivializations. Because Li is semiample, its canonical trivial metric over k is also a pure FS metric: a generating section system has maximum norm one in the valuation-ring center frame.

The composite Cmodel→XR factors through the unique extended section sbar:Spec R→XR. The two maps agree generically; their equalizer is closed by separatedness. Flatness over R makes the generic fiber schematically dense, since affine coordinate rings inject into their generic localizations by torsion freeness. Their equality is therefore scheme-theoretic, not merely agreement on a dense point set.

M2–M3. Let E be the finitely many reduced special-fiber curve components and ζE their type-II Shilov points. They form one fixed set Σ independent of i. The canonical reference curvature is
νi=ΣE ai,E δζE,  ai,E=deg_residue(Mi|E)≥0.
Divide degrees by the cleared tensor denominator for rational bundles. Positivity follows directly from pullback of the semiample Li. The special fundamental cycle has generic lengths ℓE; over a nonalgebraically closed residue field a component degree also incorporates the finite constant-field degree. In this application ℓE=1 and the constant field equals the algebraically closed residue field. These factors have been justified, rather than erased. No ordE(t) is introduced over nondiscrete R. Ordinary discretely valued test-configuration formulas retain bE=ordE(t).

Each ai,E is the fixed continuous degree functional λE(c₁(Li)) proved above. The scheme-theoretic constant composite makes λE(π*c₁(L))=0, so every ai,E→0. Finiteness of Σ gives νi(Can)→0. Let μi be the positive curvature of the actual restricted FS metric on f*Li, keeping its finite real weights. In the same local frame subtract its canonical reference. Transition terms cancel, giving the exact distribution identity
 ddᶜ(φi∘f)=μi−νi.
BE’s continuous dpsh theory and Wanner’s curve model-current identities identify these actual measures with their CLD curvature currents. Backgrounds are not replaced by an unrelated fixed ample metric.

Green correction and the net. On a connected strict affinoid V whose boundary avoids Σ, Thuillier’s Green function gζV is zero on the boundary and has interior ddᶜgζV=−δζ. Set pi=−Σζ∈Σ∩V ai,ζ gζV. Then ddᶜpi=νi in the interior and
||pi||V≤Σ ai,ζ||gζV||V→0.
This uses fixed bounded Green functions, not small mass with moving poles. The continuous functions ui=φi∘f+pi have positive CLD current, hence are Thuillier-subharmonic by Wanner4.7. Its hypotheses hold: K is complete, algebraically closed and nontrivially valued; C is smooth proper; the tested set is ordinary open; the functions are finite continuous. The ui need not decrease.

If q is harmonic on V and φ∘f≤q on ∂V, the closed boundary sets {φi∘f≥q+ε} decrease with empty intersection. Compactness and directedness supply one eventual tail where they are empty. Simultaneously ||pi||<ε. Subharmonic comparison yields ui≤q+2ε, hence φi∘f≤q+3ε. Take the decreasing original limit and then ε↓0. This uses neither Dini for a discontinuous limit nor monotonicity of ui.

For any proper strict affinoid W whose boundary might meet Σ, choose a type-II point η outside W. Thuillier’s global functions satisfy ddᶜgζ,η=δη−δζ. The correction p′i=−Σ ai,ζ gζ,η has uniform norm tending to zero and curvature νi−νi(Can)δη. The same comparison works on a neighborhood of W. Thus every harmonic comparison test holds. The bounded usc limit is subharmonic on the whole proper connected curve. It attains a finite maximum; the maximum set is closed by usc and open by Thuillier’s maximum principle, hence is the whole curve. Therefore φ∘f is constant.

All analytic fiber points. The normalization Xν→X is finite and a universal homeomorphism by Stacks0GIQ. The normal-target morphism Y→Xν satisfies every hypothesis of Stacks0AY8: properness, integral normal target, reduced source, dominating generic point, and generic global functions k(X). Its fibers are geometrically connected. A normalization fiber over a characteristic-zero field F is finite radicial with one residue field F; its reduction is Spec F. Reduction here is used only for topology and curve construction, never for a measure cycle. Consequently every geometric fiber of π is connected.

Fix one closed point z in the nonempty projective F-fiber, F=H(s). Its finite residue extension Fz/F carries the unique extended complete norm and defines one fixed analytic reference point. For any analytic y over s, separately extend H(y) to a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued Ky. For a trivial norm, first adjoin a nontrivial Gauss variable. Embed Fz into Ky over F; uniqueness of the extended norm makes this embedding isometric. This gives Ky-rational lifts of y and the same z. A family of analytic points is not placed in one common field.

The finite intersection graph of components of the reduced geometric fiber is connected. Choose closed intersection points along a component path. Within each component, take a projective characteristic-zero resolution and lift the chosen points. In dimension one its smooth proper resolution is the required curve morphism. In dimension d≥2, blow up the two distinct lifted points, then take d−1 general very ample hyperplane sections. Bertini gives smoothness; depth at closed points at least two and ample-divisor connectedness give connectedness at each stage. Impose proper intersection with both exceptional divisors. The final curve meets each: H^(d−1)·E>0 because H restricts amply to E≅P^(d−1). Its composite morphism passes through both original points. This constructs a finite chain of smooth proper connected curve morphisms in the fiber, rather than assuming a smooth embedded curve in a singular component. Curve constancy proves φ(y)=φ(z) for every y.

For unbounded φ, max(φ,−m) remains genuine in the SAME nef class: constants are nef-class psh and finite maxima are stable. Apply the bounded argument and let m→∞, including −∞ values. Define ψ(s) as the common fiber value. For each real a, {ψ≥a}=πan({φ≥a}); properness makes this closed. Hence ψ is usc. The generic trivial valuation gives generic finiteness. This proves scalar descent, not yet genuine target membership.

notes.summary: Established an unverified original-reference contact application using derived approximants on π*L+δA. Conditional only on the precisely stated countable weak-to-genuine C1, normalized PSH is homeomorphic and countable target EP follows from smooth nef compactness.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1’s all-point scalar descent, BJ12.18(ii) supplies varying-bundle finite FS approximants for an already genuine resolved potential. A subsequence is numerically dominated by actual ample bundles Bᵣ=π*L+2⁻ʳA. Adding the constant zero in the nef difference proves genuine membership in each Bᵣ; uniform rational FS approximation and summable shifts give decreasing scalars. Canonical tensor references split exactly into the original reference plus 2⁻ʳhA, with hA≥0 in fixed section frames. Thus original-frame weights are decreasing rational contact limits on the one witness, without Picard convergence or fixed π*L regularization. C1 remains an unproved countable original-class global theorem. Under it, identical divisorial valuations and actual suprema give normalized homeomorphism; BJ5.20/5.21 and5.11 give target EP without early use of5.13.
notes.text:
Use n1 with its retained hypotheses and unverified-draft status. Let ψ be its usc descended scalar and φ=π*ψ the genuine resolved potential. For an original frame e of L, put h0,e=−log||e||0. The required actual weights are be=ψ+h0,e, with be=be′−log|e/e′| and π*be=φ+π*h0,e. The pulled reference is the canonical reference on π*L by pullback of the constant model. It is not a varying Li reference. Mere scalar descent or numerical convergence would not establish local admissibility.

Original-reference contact application. Fix an actual very ample A on Y and θ=π*c₁(L). Since φ is already genuine upstairs, actual BJ12.18(ii) applies: aj∈H(Mj) decrease to φ, Mj are varying ample rational bundles, and c₁(Mj)→θ. This is the source’s varying-bundle theorem, with its12.16 proof, not a regularization theorem on the nef π*L. It does not require target EP.

Set δr=2⁻ʳ. Openness of the ample cone permits an increasing subsequence j(r) such that δrc₁(A)−(c₁(Mj(r))−θ) is ample. Constants are psh in this nef difference. Adding zero via BJ4.7 proves aj(r)∈PSH(Y,Br), where the ACTUAL rational bundle Br=π*L+δrA is ample. No Picard identification between Mj(r) and Br is made.

The aj(r) are finite continuous. BJ4.16 and Example3.9 give rational FS potentials qr on each actual Br with ||qr−aj(r)||∞<εr=4⁻ʳ. Set cr=2Σl≥r εl=(8/3)4⁻ʳ. Since aj(r)≥aj(r+1),
qr+cr−qr+1−cr+1≥2εr−εr−εr+1>0.
Thus qr+cr decreases to φ. Both approximation errors and rational shifts tend to zero.

Cover Y by frames s from a generating system of A. On D(s), its canonical reference is hA,s=maxl log|sl/s|≥0, including the branch s/s=1. Tensor multiplicativity identifies the canonical Br reference exactly as π*h0,e+δrhA,s. Therefore
wr=qr+cr+π*h0,e+δrhA,s
is the ACTUAL local FS weight in that frame, plus a rational constant. It decreases to φ+π*h0,e on the one common open π⁻¹U∩D(s): both variable terms decrease and δrhA,s↓0.

After clearing the rational tensor denominator, wr is a finite maximum of rational multiples of logarithms of regular section coefficients plus rational constants, in the original witness-chart ring. Generating sections have no common zero. At a tested point a maximizing nonzero branch is an affine support below the maximum and equal there with the SAME constant. Vanishing branches are inactive and can be removed on a smaller ordinary neighborhood; a sufficiently low rational floor is inactive on a compact smaller neighborhood. This meets the exact task-granted rational contact convention. The sequence is defined on one common chart; separate unit reductions are used to test individual continuous approximants, and finite tuples have common intersections. The construction also covers unbounded φ because12.18(ii) still gives finite continuous approximants. Floors alternatively stay in the same nef class by n1.

This proves the required original-reference application. The M1–M3 argument in n1 still uses the actual Definition4.1 net; it has not been replaced by a fictitious same-bundle net. No completed-field affine regularization is involved.

C1-original, explicitly CONDITIONAL: Over every countable algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, for original reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective X and actual ample rational L, a generically finite usc scalar ψ belongs to actual BJ Definition4.1 PSH(X,L) if its original-L weights have the original cocycle and pull back on one proper birational smooth witness to the exact local decreasing rational contact class. The theorem must retain every required compactification, projective domination and resolution-witness antecedent. It must give global membership in the ORIGINAL class, not a smooth or perturbed-class conclusion.

This C1 is not proved or inferred from another worker. n1 verifies usc and generic finiteness; the construction above verifies literal references and contact admissibility. Any upper-growth formulation is also met: sup ψ=sup φ<∞, and in an original sufficiently divisible very ample section frame h0,e is a finite affine FS maximum in the original section ratios. Thus be≤h0,e+sup ψ has the actual original upper-growth reference. One can first apply C1 to bounded floors and then use decreasing closure.

Assuming C1, pullback PSH(X,L)→PSH(Y,π*L) is onto. Forward inclusion is BJ4.7 and injectivity is analytic surjectivity. The divisorial sets are the identical valuations of the common function field, including its trivial valuation. Both BJ topologies are pointwise convergence on that same set, so this bijection is a homeomorphism. Actual analytic suprema agree. Hence normalized PSH spaces are homeomorphic. Smooth nef BJ5.20/5.21 gives compactness upstairs even though π*L is not ample. Target normalized compactness follows, and BJ5.11 gives countable target EP. BJ5.13 has not been used to obtain first membership or EP.

External primary premises are registered at nonnegative indices0,11,12,15,16, with HTTP evidence https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4. Pertinent literal units include LF2173–2297 (actual definition),2224–2351 (constants and operations),2481–2551 (topology/order),6228–6268 (varying-bundle countable regularization and proof),1692–1729 (actual Hdom bundle representation),2408–2494 (regularization and uniform FS closure),2810–2858 (compactness equivalence),2977–3070 (smooth nef EP). Units e037,e049,e050,e052,e038,e039 bind the decisive applications. Continuous operator compatibility additionally appears at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3, LF2629–2750; it is not used to invent local membership. The local-reference proof is new and unverified; C1 remains a hypothesis, not an external theorem registered with a negative index.

notes.summary: Reconstructed arbitrary-cardinality envelope descent conditional on n2’s countable EP. Separate finite obstacles and competitors descend to their own countable fields; genuine raw MA pushforward transfers orthogonality, and feasible Hdom majorants bound every arbitrary competitor.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite actual projective, normalization, model, bundle and section data descend while real weights remain real constants. Relative closure is retained inside the original nonnormal generic fiber; faithful-flat and numerical arguments preserve normality, universal homeomorphism, ampleness, nefness, central multiplicities and intersection degrees. BE’s continuous fundamental-cycle invariance and BJ compatibility give actual raw mixed MA pushforward. The nonnegative integral of f−φ transfers orthogonality, and genuine domination bounds each finite competitor. BJ4.15 decreasing Hdom nets and compact strict-epsilon feasibility then bound arbitrary genuine competitors without descending their family. Exact continuous envelope equality, PL density and varying-class closure yield EP for all ample numerical classes over arbitrary-cardinality k, conditional on C1 through n2.
notes.text:
Use n1 for numerical specialization and n2 only for its explicitly conditional countable EP. Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero, X reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective and L an actual ample rational bundle. These are unverified combined applications.

Finite fields of definition. Each chosen finite set of projective equations, affine presentations, actual bundle transition functions, sections, flag ideals, maps, action identities and generic-fiber trivializations involves finitely many coefficients. Enlarge a finitely generated subfield accordingly and take its algebraic closure inside k. It is countable in characteristic zero. Finite real weights remain the SAME real constants; an algebraic field need not encode them. Different finite competitors may need different enlargements. No arbitrary family or psh net is descended to one field.

Generation is detected by the coherent cokernel after faithfully flat extension. Reducedness and integrality are detected downstairs; over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields they are geometric. Actual ampleness and relative model ampleness descend fpqc. Descend a finite birational map with its actual source, algebra inclusion and a nonempty dense open on which it is an isomorphism. Its normal source descends normality by faithful flatness and is geometrically normal over the perfect downstairs field. Thus it is the normalization and remains so after enlargement. Universal homeomorphism descends by finite geometric fibers/residue extensions and fpqc surjectivity, or by the finite diagonal and surjectivity. The downstairs X remains geometrically unibranch. Its original nonnormal generic fiber is not silently normalized.

Actual models. Descend the model’s specified generic-fiber isomorphism and actual line bundle. Flatness over the test line is faithfully flat, equivalently torsion freeness over k0[t]. BJ1.13/1.15 characterize relative integral closure by vertical R1 and special-fiber S1. Characteristic-zero algebraically closed field extensions are regular. For the resulting noetherian local maps, flat depth and dimension formulas with regular closed fibers preserve and reflect S1; regularity preserves and reflects the generic central DVRs. Central components over the algebraically closed field are geometrically integral and remain the corresponding generic components. Hence the two vertical conditions descend and ascend. These arguments concern finite-type rings over fields, not arbitrary K°.

Alternatively form the finite relative integral closure of the descended raw model INSIDE its prescribed original generic fiber, then use the vertical criterion to identify its base extension with the prescribed model. Absolute normalization would change a nonnormal generic fiber and is not used.

At each generic central point, bE=ordE(t) is the special-fiber generic length. Flat field extension preserves it by tensoring a composition series whose residue factors remain fields at corresponding generic points. Component intersection degrees are preserved by the multivariate Hilbert polynomial and field cohomology base change. Relative nefness is preserved and reflected by n1’s curve specialization on the special projective components; ampleness is fpqc. Finite flag-ideal evaluations, divisor functions and FS maxima are the SAME scalar functions after analytic base extension, with pulled canonical references. This supplies actual finite rational PL obstacles and Hdom competitors on L.

Actual continuous raw MA. For algebraically closed trivial fields k0⊂k and p:Xkan→X0an, continuous genuine metrics on actual ample rational bundles satisfy
p*[∧j(c₁(Lj,k)+ddᶜp*φj)]=∧j(c₁(Lj)+ddᶜφj),
where p* on the left denotes measure pushforward, and the raw mass is (L1⋯Ln). The analytic projection is surjective; BJ1.9 supplies its section for field extensions.

This calibration uses BE8.3(iv), which includes the analytic fundamental cycle for smooth metrics; BE8.4/8.5 uniquely extend under uniform convergence and retain positivity and intersection mass. Semiample continuous FS limits are psh-regularizable by BE7.14. BJ4.16 gives uniform FS approximation of continuous genuine potentials on the actual rational ample bundle, and BJ7.23 identifies this measure with the genuine continuous operator on general reduced projective X. Push forward against continuous tests and pass the uniform limit. This applies on the original singular/nonnormal target, not merely its normalization.

The raw model formula is ΣE bE(ℒ1|E⋯ℒn|E)δvE, with vE=bE⁻¹ordE restricted to k(X). Fundamental-cycle lengths and finite residue-degree factors are retained. The extension argument does not define discontinuous or unbounded MA by a formal weak limit. Envelope transfer uses only continuous metrics; genuine unbounded products come separately from BJ7.18/7.19.

Every finite competitor is bounded. Fix rational f∈PL(X) and descend f,L and normalization to countable algebraically closed k0. Conditional countable EP gives the finite continuous genuine envelope φ0=P_L0(f0). A constant below min f0 is feasible. Put φ=p0*φ0; base extension of the genuine defining net gives actual continuous membership and φ≤f.

Under EP, BJ13.1 gives orthogonality independently of the desired inverse equation. With g=f0−φ0≥0, P(φ0+tg)=φ0 for 0≤t≤1, so the genuine envelope-energy derivative gives ∫g MAraw(φ0)=0. Genuine domination, BJ10.6, requires no EP or Dirac inverse equation.

Take any finite h∈Hdom(L) with h≤f. Descend its own data to a possibly larger countable algebraically closed k1⊃k0. Surjectivity gives h1≤f1. The pulled φ1 is genuine continuous. Raw pushforward and the NONNEGATIVE continuous integrand give
∫(f1−φ1) MAraw(φ1)=∫(f0−φ0) MAraw(φ0)=0.
Therefore f1=φ1 almost everywhere for MAraw(φ1), and h1≤φ1 there. Domination yields h1≤φ1 at every point, hence h≤φ after pullback. No inverse-image equality of supports is needed.

Now take an arbitrary genuine q≤f. Actual BJ4.15(iii) supplies a decreasing NET hi∈Hdom(L) with hi↓q. For rational ε>0, the closed sets {hi≥f+ε} on compact Xan decrease with empty intersection. Directed finite-intersection compactness makes them eventually empty. Thus hi−ε is a finite feasible Hdom competitor; rational translation preserves that class. Each is bounded separately by φ, even though it may need its own field. Take the decreasing limit and then ε↓0. This gives q≤φ. Consequently the exact unregularized envelope identity is
P_L(f)=p0*P_L0(f0).
It is continuous and genuine. No simultaneous descent of arbitrary q or its net was assumed.

PL density and the elementary envelope Lipschitz estimate ||P(f)−P(g)||∞≤||f−g||∞ extend continuity and genuine membership to all finite continuous obstacles. BJ5.17 gives EP for each rational ample class. For any real ample numerical α, choose rational ample ωj→α with ωj−α ample. Openness of the ample cone permits a small positive displacement toward a fixed rational ample direction. Constants are psh in each nef difference, so PSH(α)⊂PSH(ωj). The usc supremum of any bounded-above α-family is ωj-psh by EP there. Actual varying-class closure then makes it α-psh. This proves arbitrary-cardinality EP for every ample numerical class, conditional only on countable EP from n2.

The EXACT unchanged original P16.1 is not solved. All seven original family axes and the completion criterion are retained in the byte-preserved input and task file. The present retained domain is reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective X over arbitrary algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k, with an actual ample rational L and arbitrary-support finite-dual-energy targets. No arbitrary-valued-field, nonample, nonprojective or nonalgebraizable extension is asserted. Use n1–n3 only within their stated conditionality. All combined arguments remain unverified drafts.

Normalization after EP. A finite birational universal homeomorphism ν:Xν→X induces an analytic homeomorphism: each radicial fiber has one analytic point with its unique residue-field norm, and a proper continuous bijection of compact Hausdorff spaces is a homeomorphism. Topology alone does not prove genuine psh descent.

Here is the required explicit blowup. Let B=ν*OXν and J=AnnOX(B/OX). The conductor is nonzero by clearing denominators of finitely many integral birational generators. Choose an ample twist A and a nonzero section a∈H⁰(J⊗A). In a frame define I=aB⊂OX. Frame changes are units, so these coherent ideals glue. On an integral affine chart A0⊂B0, I=aB0 and Iᵐ=aᵐB0 for m≥1. Its Rees algebra is A0⊕⊕m≥1 aᵐB0tᵐ. The single chart D+(at) covers Proj: every degree-one abt satisfies a monic equation whose degree-j coefficients contain (at)ʲ. A homogeneous prime containing at therefore contains every degree-one generator and is not a Proj point. Its degree-zero localization is B0 because (abt)/(at)=b. Thus BlI(X)=Xν scheme-theoretically, and these identities glue. No incorrect claim that the conductor pullback itself is invertible is needed.

Only AFTER n3’s conditional target EP, choose θm=(1+1/m)c₁(L)>c₁(L). BJ5.13 now gives the genuine homeomorphism ν*:PSH(X,L)→PSH(Xν,ν*L). Its approaching classes lie on the TARGET and have EP. The lemma was not used to obtain first target membership or EP. Actual suprema agree, and continuous potentials correspond under the analytic homeomorphism.

Actual finite-energy operator and transport. BJ’s conventions and Section7 cover general reduced, possibly nonnormal, projective varieties. Its genuine operator exists independently of EP. Let V=(Lⁿ)>0 and MAraw_L(ψ)=(c₁(L)+ddᶜψ)ⁿ; the probability calibration is MA_L=MAraw_L/V. It is not a substitute inverse law.

BJ7.2, equation7.5, gives normalization pullback equality for actual mixed energy pairings. BJ7.19, equation7.18, gives ν* of the genuine raw mixed measure upstairs equal to the mixed measure downstairs, with ν* here denoting measure pushforward. This holds for genuine signed finite-energy entries in the source’s stated scope, including unbounded entries. At model level normalization has degree one and pushes its fundamental cycle to [X]; at generic vertical DVRs it is an isomorphism, preserving bE and projected intersection coefficients. For general entries the source extends the actual symmetric pairing by monotone energy continuity and defines the Radon measure by testing PL functions. PL density identifies measures. An arbitrary formal weak limit is not used to manufacture an operator.

The energy is E_L(ψ)=⟨(c₁(L),ψ)ⁿ⁺¹⟩/((n+1)V); E1 consists of genuine psh potentials with energy greater than −∞. Floors pull back exactly and their raw pairings agree. Decreasing energy continuity yields E_L(ψ)=E_ν*L(ν*ψ), including −∞. After onto PSH, this proves onto E1. Weak topologies use identical divisorial valuations; strong E1 topologies additionally use this same energy, so both transport. No I-Cauchy completion creates a potential.

The exact raw target condition is: η is a positive Radon measure, η(Xan)=V, and
E∨_L(η/V)=supψ∈E1 [E_L(ψ)−∫ψ d(η/V)]<∞.
BJ9.20 on irreducible general X equates it with integrability of EVERY genuine E1 potential. There is no skeleton or support restriction. Transport η through the analytic normalization homeomorphism. Mass, integrability and dual energy agree by ordinary change of variables and energy equality; actual mixed-product pushforward transports solutions. Nilpotents are removed only for the fiber topology in n1, never when computing model fundamental cycles.

Conditional existence with every replacement. The decisive general-variety theorem is BJ12.8, which equates ample EP and onto genuine finite-energy MA; its smooth corollary12.9 is not substituted.

Compactness: target normalized PSH compactness is equivalent to EP by5.11. On countable targets n2 transfers it from smooth NEF compactness under C1. On arbitrary-cardinality targets n3 establishes EP by separate finite-obstacle and finite-competitor descent. No metrizability or countable cofinal net is assumed.

Envelopes: they are genuine in the original ample class by the exact envelope equality in n3, PL density, uniform closure and varying-class closure. Orthogonality transfers by the nonnegative integral of f−φ, without a support-preimage assertion. Wu’s new v1 envelope proof expressly invokes its resolved-nef Proposition2.24 and weak/global Theorem6.5; its printed conclusion is not independent verification of C1.

Differentiation: BJ8.5 gives, for genuine E1 ψ and PL g, E↓(ψ+tg)=E(ψ)+t∫g MA_L(ψ)+O(t²). BJ8.6 gives continuous-test differentiation. Under EP the outer energy equals E(P_L(ψ+tg)). This is the actual general-variety energy and operator, not an auxiliary probability construction.

Attainment: choose a normalized dual maximizing sequence. Its dual gaps J_(η/V) tend to zero; BJ9.11 bounds its ordinary J-energy. Compactness gives a subnet and lower semicontinuity keeps its limit in E1. BJ9.19 gives L¹(η/V) convergence on this bounded-energy set. Energy upper semicontinuity then gives an ACTUAL maximizer. A formal maximizing sequence without compactness would not suffice.

Equation: for a maximizer ψ and any continuous g, the genuine envelope P_L(ψ+tg) lies between ψ−|t|||g||∞ and ψ+|t|||g||∞, hence is E1. Since it is at most ψ+tg, maximality gives
E(P_L(ψ+tg))−∫(ψ+tg)d(η/V)≤E(ψ)−∫ψ d(η/V).
Use both signs of t and the outer derivative. Then ∫g MA_L(ψ)=∫g d(η/V) for every continuous test, so MAraw_L(ψ)=η as actual Radon measures.

Comparison and uniqueness: genuine BJ7.40–7.44 supplies finite-energy winning-locus locality and comparison using maxima, equal raw mass and decreasing continuity. BJ10.4 gives uniqueness modulo one real constant from genuine E1 estimates and divisorial order; BJ10.6 supplies domination without EP. These assertions remain on the general-variety scope.

The raw variational objective VE_L(ψ)−∫ψ dη changes by c(V−η(Xan)) under addition of c. Thus exact mass V is necessary for constant invariance. Positive ample volume permits the calibrated probability measure η/V; no zero-volume or nonample claim follows. In dimension zero X=Spec k, the empty product has raw mass one and the equation is immediate.

The resulting equation theorem is conditional ONLY on C1 as precisely stated in n2: the countable original-class weak-to-genuine GLOBAL theorem for the admissible original-frame weights, retaining all geometric witness antecedents. The local-reference/contact application is proved in n2 using varying actual ample bundles. C1 itself is not proved here or assumed from independent Runge work. Consequently the unchanged completion criterion remains unmet and candidate=false.
